_note: Reference for authors. Copy the SHAPE, not the words. Ref keys must exist in docs/lld/research/*.jsonl. The `line`/`dumb` strings follow the writing rules in AUTHORING.md.

group.line: RRF fuses dense, keyword and graph rankings, a cross-encoder reorders the top 100, and every answer sentence carries a checked citation.
group.dumb: Three searchers each hand back their own ranked list. We merge the lists by rank, so a result that several searchers like rises to the top. A stricter reader then re-orders the best hundred, and the answer is written only from what it kept, with a link to the exact passage.

kn_fuse.line:
RRF merges three ranked lists:
score = sum 1 / (60 + rank)
kn_fuse.dumb: Each searcher gives its own ranking. For every passage we add up 1 divided by (60 plus its position in each list). A passage ranked well by two searchers beats one ranked first by only one. No score scaling is needed because only positions are used.
kn_fuse.inn: Three ranked lists per query: dense top 100 (kn_vec), keyword top 100 (kn_bm25), graph top 50 (kn_graph). Each item is (chunk_id, rank).
kn_fuse.out: One fused list of up to 100 chunk ids with fused score, plus each chunk's per-source ranks kept for the trace.
kn_fuse.store: Reads nothing (stateless function). Writes one retrieval-trace row per query to the observability store.
kn_fuse.fail: A source that times out is dropped and the trace is marked degraded. If all three fail it returns an empty list and kn_abst abstains.
kn_fuse.req: company-os-v2.md section 2, block B3: 'answer with citations; respect source permissions'
kn_fuse.hard: k=60 is the published default; re-tune per tenant only after 500 labelled queries exist.

deep.purpose: Combine rankings whose scores are not comparable (cosine, BM25, graph walk) into one order without learning weights.
expected: A passage found by dense and keyword search outranks one found by a single source
Output is deterministic for identical input lists
not_expected: It does not look at passage text or score values, only ranks
It does not apply permissions; kn_perm already filtered the inputs

algorithm.name: Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF)
algorithm.formula: RRF(d) = sum over sources s of 1 / (k + rank_s(d)),  k = 60
steps: For each source list, assign rank 1..n by position
For every distinct chunk id, sum 1/(k+rank) over the sources that returned it
Break ties by the best single-source rank, then by chunk id for determinism
Sort descending and keep the top 100

definitions: rank_s(d): 1-based position of d in s, absent if d not returned
math.formula_full: RRF(d) = sum_{s in S, d in s} 1 / (k + rank_s(d))
math.derivation: A reciprocal of rank gives steep reward at the top and a long flat tail. Adding k flattens the head so one first place cannot dominate two second places. Summing across sources rewards agreement.
math.worked_example: k=60. Chunk A: dense rank 1, keyword rank 3 -> 1/61 + 1/63 = 0.01639 + 0.01587 = 0.03226. Chunk B: dense rank 2 only -> 1/62 = 0.01613. A beats B.
math.complexity: O(N log N) in the number of distinct chunks N <= 250; under 1 ms.
failure_modes: One source returns near-duplicates and floods the top: dedupe by chunk fingerprint before fusion
A source with systematically bad rank 1: keep a per-source weight of 1.0 and only change it behind an eval
math.calibration: Keep k=60 until a tenant has 500 labelled queries; then sweep k in {20,40,60,100} offline on recall@20 and ship only a gain above 2 points.

alternatives.name: Weighted score sum (min-max normalised)
alternatives.why_rejected: Needs score normalisation that drifts with corpus and query; RRF has no scale to tune.

alternatives.name: Learned fusion (LambdaMART)
alternatives.why_rejected: Needs labelled data per tenant; kept as a later upgrade behind the eval gate.

security: Inputs are already permission-filtered; fusion adds no new document ids, so it cannot widen access
Trace stores chunk ids only, never text, so the trace store holds no tenant content

performance.scaling: Stateless; scales horizontally. The cost at 10x load is the three upstream searches, not the merge.

edge_cases: Empty list from one source: skipped, trace marked degraded
Same chunk appears twice in one list: only the best rank counts
All lists empty: returns empty, kn_abst abstains
Duplicate content under two chunk ids: fingerprint dedupe keeps the one with the higher best rank

tests.name: agreement wins
tests.given: A: ranks 1 and 3; B: rank 1 in one list only
tests.expect: A ranked above B with score 0.03226

tests.name: deterministic ties
tests.given: two chunks with equal fused score
tests.expect: order by best single-source rank then chunk id, identical across 100 runs

tests.name: source outage
tests.expect: fused list from two sources, trace.degraded = true

cost_levers: Pure arithmetic, no model call; the fusion cutoff of 100 caps the cross-encoder bill downstream
feedback_events: Click and 'was this useful' on cited passages feed the per-tenant recall@k eval set

papers.key_idea: Rank-only fusion with k=60 beats most single rankers and learned fusion on TREC and similar sets.
papers.how: Adopted unchanged as the default; k becomes a per-tenant parameter only behind an offline eval.

deep.industry: Elasticsearch, OpenSearch and Qdrant ship RRF as a built-in hybrid fusion mode.

edges.d: Ordered chunk ids with fused score and per-source ranks. Sent to the cross-encoder which reduces to top 8.
